resources.string: Many controllers in X-input mode send their Home (guide) button as a button Android ignores. Inside Tandem it always works like Home. To make it work in games and other apps too, switch on \"Tandem: Controller Home button\" in Android\'s Accessibility settings (A opens them; if it is greyed out, allow restricted settings in Tandem\'s App info first). Tandem then looks only at that one button, only from external controllers; the built-in controls are never touched.
What holding a controller\'s Home button does: Tandem\'s game switcher, or Android\'s recent apps (needs Controller Home button on; without it, the game switcher).

Nintendo button labels: swaps A/B and X/Y for this controller only, so the button printed A confirms. Use it for Switch-style pads in X-input mode. It applies inside Tandem; the built-in controls and other controllers are unaffected, and Swap A and B above still applies on top. Emulators have their own per-controller button mapping in their settings.

Pair a Bluetooth controller or plug one in and it shows up here, with its own Nintendo button labels switch (swap A/B and X/Y for that controller only). The built-in controls follow Swap A and B above.
Pair or plug in a controller, it appears here

Which controller plays as the built-in one, in every emulator, mid-game included: games keep listening to the built-in controls and Tandem passes the chosen controller\'s buttons and sticks to them. The built-in controls keep working too (also in Quick settings). A controller connecting during a game offers itself on the bottom screen: press its A or Start. Disconnecting it goes back to the built-in controls.

Always use a connected controller: one that connects plays as the built-in controller at once, without asking. Leave it off to play two players: the controller then stays a controller of its own, and the emulator needs it mapped as Player 2.
Opens the highlighted item or plays the game; A on buttons and rows.
Goes back, or closes a menu or panel.
The options menu for the highlighted game, system, folder or app; a long press on the touch screen.
Search, or swap the two screens on the icon grid, as X button says. Deletes a letter on the keyboard.
The Start panel; in Settings it closes Settings, and in forms it confirms.
Brightness, volume, Wi-Fi, Battery saver and the other quick tiles.
Every game that is open, to resume or close.
The game switcher again, on buttons pressed together: Select and Start, unless you change it.
Jumps to a random game you have never played. Also Undo on a message, and Select in the apps.
Private mode off: turns it on at once. On: shows hidden games after your PIN, or tucks them away.
The previous system, collection, Settings page or Stats tab; bigger icons on the grid.
The next system, collection, Settings page or Stats tab; smaller icons on the grid.
In a list of games the previous letter (or year, rating), elsewhere a page up; the Recently played strip on the grid.
In a list of games the next letter (or year, rating), elsewhere a page down.
On the home screen: Pip, the quick settings and your notifications. Shares its button with Page down unless you change it.
Adds the highlighted game to your favourites, or takes it out again. No button until you give it one.
A screenshot of the game playing on the other screen, saved to ROMs/screenshots, as the companion\'s Screenshot does. Works while Tandem is in front.
A 15-second clip of the game playing on the other screen, or stops the one recording, as the companion\'s Clip does. Works while Tandem is in front.
A controller\'s Home (guide) button inside Tandem: a tap is Home, a hold does what Hold the Home button says.
%1$s needs a single button, not a chord or a hold
%1$s is %2$s: it can\'t be part of a chord or a hold
%1$s is %2$s, which always needs a button: give %2$s another one first
Every command back on the button it came with.
Every command goes back on the button it came with, Swap A and B and Swap X and Y included. Undo brings your buttons back.
Every button is on its default already
Every button is back on its default
Nothing pressed: %1$s stays as it was
Press the new button, or several together for a chord. Hold one button for a hold.
%1$s is %2$s. Swapped, %3$s takes it and %2$s moves to %4$s.
%1$s is %2$s. Swapped, %3$s takes it and %2$s is left with no button.
The Deck types into a game on the top screen. This game plays on the bottom one, so there is nothing for it to do here.
Tap Shift, Ctrl or Alt for the next key; hold to lock it
Keys and the pointer go straight into Android\'s input service, in a few milliseconds
Android kept Tandem from the input service, so each key runs an input command: it takes a moment, and clicks land where the pad\'s cursor points
Start Shizuku and allow Tandem, then open the Deck again
Drag to point · tap to click · two fingers for a right click or to scroll
How far the game\'s pointer goes for a finger\'s movement on the Deck\'s trackpad. Quick swipes always go further than slow, careful ones.
The keyboard the Deck opens with: the full keyboard, or the compact one with the WASD cluster and mouse buttons. Switch any time with the chips on the Deck.
A soft click for each key and tap on the Deck.
A tiny buzz for each key and tap on the Deck.
Press A or Start on it. It takes over the built-in controls in this game.
Press A or Start on %1$s to play with it
This build of Tandem has no controller helper.
This device has no built-in controller to stand in for.
Needs Shizuku or root: a game only reads the built-in controller, and only they can feed it.
